How do I undo the last git commit?

It depends what you want:

- Keep the changes, unstage them: `git reset --soft HEAD~1`
- Keep changes in the working tree: `git reset HEAD~1` (mixed)
- Throw the changes away entirely: `git reset --hard HEAD~1` (dangerous!)

Only use --hard if you're sure — it deletes the work in that commit.

How do I rename all .txt files to .md in bash?

Use a simple loop:

for f in *.txt; do
  mv "$f" "${f%.txt}.md"
done

${f%.txt} strips the extension. Quote "$f" to handle filenames with spaces.

What's the difference between var, let, and const in JavaScript?

const can't be reassigned (use it by default), let can be reassigned but is block-scoped, and var is function-scoped with hoisting quirks. Modern rule of thumb: const unless you know the value will change, then let. Avoid var in new code.

What is a REST API and how does it work?

A REST API is a way for programs to talk over HTTP. Resources have URLs (like /users), and HTTP methods say what to do: GET reads, POST creates, PUT/PATCH updates, DELETE removes. The server usually returns JSON. It's the standard way web apps, mobile apps, and servers communicate.

How do I make a Minecraft mod?

Mods are written in Java. Pick a mod loader first: Fabric (lightweight, updates fast), Forge (huge classic ecosystem), or NeoForge (the community continuation of Forge). Then set up a project with that loader's official example mod on GitHub, write your mod classes, and run the Gradle task `gradlew runClient` to launch a test Minecraft client. When it works, `gradlew build` produces a .jar you drop into your mods folder. Start tiny: add one item or block, get it loading, then grow.

What's the difference between Forge, Fabric, and NeoForge?

They're the three main mod loaders — frameworks that let mods hook into Minecraft. Forge is the oldest with the biggest library of classic mods. NeoForge is the community fork that continues Forge (Forge itself is largely unmaintained now). Fabric is newer, lighter, simpler, and updates to new Minecraft versions fastest. For new projects many people pick Fabric or NeoForge. All use Java and Gradle.

How do I make a Minecraft server plugin?

Plugins run on Bukkit/Spigot/Paper servers, not vanilla. Use Java with the Paper API. Set up a Gradle or Maven project depending on paper-api, implement the JavaPlugin class, register listeners and commands in onEnable(), build a .jar, and drop it in the server's plugins folder. Paper has good docs at docs.papermc.io with examples.

Can I make a Minecraft launcher in Python?

Yes. A launcher downloads and runs Minecraft for you. The core flow: fetch Mojang's version manifest, pick a version, read its JSON, download the client jar, assets, and libraries, build the classpath, then spawn `java -cp <classpath> net.minecraft.client.main.Main --version <version>`. The minecraft-launcher-lib Python package handles most of this. Wrap it in a tkinter or PyQt GUI and you have a real launcher.

How do I make a simple command in a Paper plugin?

How do I test my Minecraft mod?

While developing, run the Gradle task that launches a test client: `gradlew runClient` (Fabric, Forge, and NeoForge all provide it). That boots a dev Minecraft with your mod loaded — the fastest test loop. When you're happy, `gradlew build` produces the release .jar in build/libs, and you drop it into a normal installation's mods folder. Server plugins go in a Paper server's plugins folder.

What's the difference between a mod and a plugin?

A mod changes the game itself by injecting code into Minecraft — new items, blocks, mechanics — made with Forge/Fabric/NeoForge. A plugin runs on top of a Bukkit/Spigot/Paper server and adds server-side features (commands, permissions, minigames) without changing the client. New items and blocks for players = a mod; server commands and gameplay tweaks = a plugin.

Test with runClient, then build. Small mods update in minutes; big ones take real work.

How does a game loop work?

A game loop repeats forever: (1) read player input, (2) update the game state (move things, check collisions) using the time since the last frame (delta time), (3) draw the frame, (4) wait a little and repeat. In tkinter you use root.after() to schedule ticks; in pyglet you schedule an update function that receives dt. Delta time keeps speed consistent regardless of frame rate.

How does collision detection work in games?

The simplest and most common is AABB (axis-aligned bounding box): treat every object as a box and check whether two boxes overlap on all three axes. For movement, you move one axis at a time and resolve collisions per axis, which lets the player slide along walls and land on floors. For a voxel world, you check which blocks the player's box overlaps and treat those as solid.

How do I generate 3D terrain like Minecraft?

Use noise. Pick a height for every (x, z) column from layered value or Perlin noise (add multiple octaves at different frequencies for hills and detail). Then fill downward: grass on top, dirt below, stone underneath, and sprinkle trees on the surface. For the renderer, build a mesh of only the block faces that touch air — that keeps the polygon count low. That's exactly how the `game: voxel` template works.

How do I make a platformer game?

Core pieces: a player rectangle with gravity (velocity += gravity * dt each frame) and a jump (set upward velocity when on the ground), solid platforms to collide with using AABB per-axis resolution, and camera follow. Add a level made of rectangles, spikes that kill, and a goal. Start with a single flat platform and one moving character, then add enemies and scrolling.
